q: A job has `ingest → transform → publish`. `transform` fails after `ingest` ran for two hours. You fix the bug. What is the cheapest way to finish the run?
o: Repair the run: `transform` and `publish` re-run, `ingest` keeps its result
Create a new job with only `transform` and `publish`
e: A repair run re-executes the unsuccessful tasks and their dependents within the same run. Tasks that succeeded are not run again.

q: A clean-up task must run after its upstream tasks finish, whether they succeeded or failed. Which Run if setting do you use?
e: `ALL_DONE` only requires that all upstream tasks are finished, with any result. With the default `ALL_SUCCESS` the task would be Upstream failed after a failure.

q: Partner files land in a volume at unpredictable times, sometimes twice a day, sometimes not for a week. How should the ingestion job be triggered?
o: A file arrival trigger on the volume
A table update trigger on the target table
e: A file arrival trigger starts a run when new files appear, so there are no empty polling runs and no waiting for the next schedule slot.

q: Task `ingest` runs `dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="new_rows", value=n)`. How does an If/else condition task downstream refer to that value?
e: Task values are referenced as `{{tasks.<task_key>.values.<key>}}`. Job parameters use `{{job.parameters.<name>}}`.

q: A task has `timeout_seconds: 3600` and `max_retries: 2`. The first attempt hangs. What happens?
o: The task runs until someone cancels it
The attempt is stopped after one hour and the task is retried; each attempt has its own one-hour limit
The whole job is stopped and no retry happens
Only a duration warning is sent
e: The timeout applies to each attempt. A timed-out attempt counts as a failure and can be retried. A duration warning threshold only notifies.
